newsitem.title: USA: Crew escape Federal Express plane crash in Newark.
newsitem.headline: Crew escape Federal Express plane crash in Newark.

text.p: Five crew members had an amazing escape when their Federal Express MD-11 cargo plane crash landed at Newark International Airport early on Thursday, flipped over and burst into flames, airport officials said.

The five flight crew crawled to safety through a cockpit window after the cargo jet overturned on landing at 1:35 a.m. EDT (0535 GMT) about 200 yards (metres) from a terminal, a spokesman for the New York/New Jersey Port Authority said.

"It was a very hard landing," Port Authority spokesman Allen Morrison said. "The plane, on impact, flipped over and began to burn. All five crew members on board were able to crawl out the cockpit window.
"They all walked away from it," Morrison said. They were treated for unspecified injuries at Elizabeth General Hospital in Elizabeth, N.J.
At 4:15 a.m. EDT, Morrison said firefighters were still battling the burning wreckage with foam and the airport, one of the busiest in the U.S., was closed indefinitely.
Once the fire was out, crews would clear debris from the crash site and National Transportation Safety Board investigators would sift the wreckage, Morrison said.
"Pieces of the plane are scattered on the runway," Morrison added. CBS radio reported that the fuselage was missing both wings and the tail section.
They reported that an eye-witness had seen flames coming from the cargo plane before it landed.
The wide-body aircraft was arriving from Anchorage, Alaska, according to Warren Perkins, a Federal Express Hub Command Center agent, who spoke in a telephone interview from Memphis.
"It is one of the larger types of aircraft in our fleet," Perkins said.

Fedex is the world's biggest cargo airline, carrying 3.77 million scheduled freight tonnes in 1996, ahead of Lufthansa with 2.88 million tonnes, according to the International Air Transport Association (IATA).
Fedex, which has 23 MD-11s in its fleet, is also the biggest U.S. domestic cargo carrier, with 2.97 million tonnes last year, ahead of UPS with 2.60 million.
